title: Gotham Operational Identity — implementation review
lede: Primary operational nouns regain Gotham while controls, dates, statuses, descriptions, product metadata, and prose remain on Geist.

stats.n: 18 primary-identity hooks plus one family-only shared treatment
Before and after captures have identical dimensions and row structure
Geist plus Gotham Medium and Bold verified in the browser

sections.heading: Matched identity hierarchy
sections.note: Same fixture data, viewport, dimensions, weights, sizes, colors, spacing, and component geometry. The only visual variable is the primary-identity font family.

pairs.title: Bookings, selected equipment, and people
pairs.sub: A source-equivalent review fixture isolates the shared typography decision across three representative operational surfaces.
pairs.beforeCap: Source-control baseline: row titles, asset tags, SKU names, and person names inherit Geist with their supporting metadata.
pairs.afterCap: Current source: primary labels use Gotham; dates, locations, status, rank, elapsed time, and supporting product/context text stay Geist.

changesNote: This is an identity correction, not a global font swap. The body remains Geist and the new treatment sets no size, weight, tracking, color, or layout property.

changes.h: Primary row identity had no semantic font role
changes.was: Rows outside semantic headings and card titles inherited the body face, so booking names, selected equipment, report links, and some person-name rows quietly drifted to Geist.
changes.now: A family-only .brand-identity treatment gives those nouns the same Gotham role already used by page, detail, card, item-table, booking-list, and user-list identity.

changes.h: Shared seams now carry the decision
changes.was: Parallel surfaces restated only weight and size, leaving font choice accidental and route-specific.
changes.now: The shared Item title and report entity link carry Gotham, with direct hooks for item booking history, equipment selection/review, organization rows, overdue rankings, and app-activity people rows.

changes.was: A broad container-level font change would also brand dates, statuses, descriptions, and controls, making dense operational screens noisier.
changes.now: Only the identifying noun changes family. The source contract guards the body face and representative metadata lines.

verification: 16 focused typography/detail-header tests pass, including four new brand-identity source contracts.
TypeScript and lint: npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false, focused ESLint, and full npm run lint pass.
Production-shaped build: npm run build:app compiles and generates all 236 static pages.
Docs and source hygiene: codemaps regenerated, npm run verify:docs and git diff --check pass.
Browser measurement: Geist, Gotham Medium, and Gotham Bold all load; the matched booking title glyph width changes from 189.1px to 200.0px while capture geometry remains unchanged.
Authenticated baseline: production /users/org-chart currently computes person names as Geist, confirming the deployed drift this local source corrects.
notes: The paired images are local source-equivalent typography proof, not a deployed after-capture. The authenticated production app remains unchanged until the normal release flow runs.

An authenticated current-source route could not be rendered without a local session; the review therefore isolates the exact family delta with repository font files and separately verifies the real production baseline.
Schedule assignee labels and battery-family supporting labels remain Geist until those surfaces make a separate primary-versus-supporting hierarchy decision.
